summary: Smoky, chilli-hot grilled goat meat chopped into bite-size pieces and tossed with onions and peppers in a fiery sauce.
story: Asun is a Yoruba party favourite, usually made with goat meat that is boiled until tender, grilled for smoky edges and tossed in a peppery sauce. It is commonly served at celebrations and in bars as a spicy small plate.

steps.title: Season and boil
steps.text: Put the goat in a pot with the quartered onion, garlic, thyme, cubes and salt. Add just enough water to barely cover. Cover and simmer gently for 50 to 70 minutes until a knife slides in easily but the meat is not falling off the bone.

steps.title: Reduce the stock
steps.text: Remove the meat and keep it. Boil the remaining stock hard for a few minutes to reduce it to about 1/3 cup, which will add concentrated flavour later.

steps.title: Dry and grill
steps.text: Pat the goat dry and spread it on a tray. Grill under a hot oven grill or over charcoal for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until the edges are browned and slightly charred and the surface looks dry.

steps.title: Blend the peppers
steps.text: Blend the bell peppers, scotch bonnets, the chopped onion and the garlic coarsely, only until chunky. Do not add water.

steps.title: Cook the sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the sliced onion for 2 minutes. Add the pepper mix and cook over medium-high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the water has cooked away and the sauce thickens and glistens with oil.

steps.title: Toss together
steps.text: Stir in the ginger and the reduced stock, then season. Add the grilled goat and toss over heat for 2 minutes until each piece is glossy and coated. Garnish with spring onion and serve warm.

tips: Goat can be tough. Boil it until just tender before grilling, as the grill only adds colour.
Pat the meat very dry before grilling for better char.
The scotch bonnet gives the heat; remove seeds for a milder dish.
Asun reheats well in a hot pan.

swaps.swap: Use lamb shoulder or beef shin with the same method. The flavour is milder, and lamb will cook slightly faster.
Habanero is the closest match; for less heat use a milder red chilli.

name: Asun (Spicy Goat Meat)
